primary_claim: Feature hedging — MSE reconstruction loss causing SAEs to merge correlated-but-untracked features into their latents — occurs in real LLM SAEs, evidenced by 40-50% of the change to existing latents falling in the subspace of newly added latents as an SAE is grown, versus ~2% for a random subspace baseline.

effect.metric: % of existing-latent delta projecting onto newly-added-latent subspace, vs random-subspace baseline

contradicts_or_qualifies: prior findings that SAEs underperform on probing (arXiv 2502.16681) and steering (arXiv 2501.17148) — the authors say hedging may help explain this underperformance
stated_future_work: more studies of larger and more realistic toy models to clarify why snap loss does not help on real LLM SAEs
develop a metric to determine the level of hedging in a given SAE without growing it
limitations_stated: snap loss solves hedging in toy models only if the amount of hedging is small; fails when hedging is large
snap loss shows no obvious benefit on real LLM SAEs in pareto/SAEBench comparisons
no ground-truth features exist in real LLM SAEs, so hedging cannot be directly measured, only inferred
authors are uncertain how to interpret the SAE decoder bias norm trend with width
quote: We see the behavior predicted by hedging is borne out, with about 40-50% of the change in existing latents happening in the subspace of the newly added latents.
